solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Intervals of quiet amid chatter (4)

indicatorNotes.amid: something amid something else sits in the middle of it

blocks.note: to gas is to chatter idly
p (piano) is the musical mark for quiet

annotation.surface: Pauses in a noisy conversation.
annotation.walkthrough: "Intervals of quiet" reads as one phrase, but "of" belongs to the definition's side and "quiet" is only the P.
annotation.definitionFit: Gaps are intervals, breaks between one thing and the next.

entries.clue: Grand antique dish lastly edged in gilt (4-6)

indicatorNotes.lastly: takes the last letter of edged

blocks.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
antique means old
a plate is a dish
last letter of edged

annotation.surface: An old serving dish with a gilded rim.
annotation.walkthrough: "Edged in gilt" looks like one description of the dish, but "in" just links the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Something gold-plated is covered in a thin layer of gold, which is what gilt means.

entries.clue: Authors crossing river, small and stony (9)

indicatorNotes.crossing: the authors stretch across the river, holding it inside

blocks.note: a pen is a writer, as in a hired pen
the Nile is the river
S is short for small

annotation.surface: Writers wading over a small, rocky stream.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stony" looks like it describes the river, but it is the definition: stony broke means penniless.
annotation.definitionFit: Stony, short for stony broke, means having no money at all.

entries.clue: Crater’s inside hardens and contracts (10)

indicatorNotes.inside: the crater goes inside the word for hardens

blocks.note: to inure is to toughen or harden
a crater is a dent or hollow

annotation.surface: The inside of a crater sets hard and shrinks.
annotation.walkthrough: "Contracts" looks like a verb for shrinking, but it is the noun: formal agreements.
annotation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal contract, such as one binding an apprentice to a master.

entries.clue: Pile family’s linen on the table (7)

blocks.note: nap is the raised pile on cloth
kin is family; with the 's, KIN'S

annotation.surface: Heap the household's table linen in a pile.
annotation.walkthrough: "Pile" looks like a verb for stacking, but it is the nap of fabric.
annotation.definitionFit: Napkins are pieces of table linen set at each place.

entries.clue: Former noble that is first to retire (7)

indicatorNotes.first to: takes the first letter of retire

blocks.note: an earl is a nobleman
i.e. is Latin id est, that is
first letter of retire

annotation.surface: An ex-aristocrat who was the first to step down.
annotation.walkthrough: "Former noble" reads as one phrase, an ex-peer, but "Former" is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Former and earlier both mean coming before in time.

entries.clue: Issue created by returned egg deliveries (4-4,6)

annotation.definition: Issue created by returned egg deliveries

blocks.note: the surface suggests a problem arising; issue is also offspring, children
not parcels sent back but eggs fertilised in a lab and returned to the womb, then delivered as babies

annotation.surface: Offspring of eggs that were sent back.
annotation.walkthrough: The picture is of parcels returned to sender; really the eggs are taken out, fertilised in the lab, and put back in the womb, and the births that follow are the deliveries.
annotation.definitionFit: Test-tube babies are children (issue) born after IVF, where fertilised eggs are returned to the mother.

entries.clue: Blade that turns both ways (5)

indicatorNotes.turns both ways: the word reads the same forwards and backwards

blocks.note: the definition end of the clue: a spinning blade, like a helicopter's
the wordplay end: five letters that come out the same read from either end

annotation.surface: A blade that can spin in either direction.
annotation.walkthrough: A rotor really does turn, so the indicator doubles as a fair description of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating blade assembly of a helicopter, or a single blade of it.

entries.clue: Boot bag (4)

blocks.note: the verb: to boot someone out is to dismiss them
the noun: a large bag of coarse cloth, as for potatoes or coal

annotation.walkthrough: "Boot" suggests a shoe or a car's luggage space next to "bag"; here it is the verb, to dismiss.
annotation.definitionFit: To boot or sack someone is to fire them; a sack is also a large bag.

entries.clue: Con artist’s trick, men traced to her shuffles (5-4,5)

indicatorNotes.shuffles: mixes the letters of the words before it

blocks.note: these fourteen letters rearranged

annotation.surface: A swindler's trick: men are tracked down to her, and she shuffles.
annotation.walkthrough: "Shuffles" suits the card game in the answer, which is why it hides so well as the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Three-card monte is a street con where the mark bets on finding one card among three.

entries.clue: Start needing a meal (5)

indicatorNotes.needing: needing a means lacking an A, so the A is taken out

blocks.note: to launch is to start
the A is removed

annotation.surface: Beginning the day hungry for a meal.
annotation.walkthrough: "Needing a meal" reads as hunger, but "needing" means going without, and "a" is the letter dropped.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain definition by example: of all the meals, this is the one taken at midday.

entries.clue: Sponging relations housed by soldiers in charge (9)

indicatorNotes.housed by: the relations are given a home inside the soldiers-in-charge letters

blocks.note: paras are paratroopers
it is slang for sex, sexual relations
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

annotation.surface: Freeloading relatives put up by the army commanders.
annotation.walkthrough: "Relations" wants to be relatives, the family scroungers of the surface; here it is IT.
annotation.definitionFit: Sponging means living off others, which is what a parasite does.

entries.clue: Perhaps two clergymen leading politicians (5,9)

indicatorNotes.Perhaps: two is only an example of a prime number

blocks.note: two is a prime number
ministers are clergymen

annotation.surface: A pair of vicars at the head of political life.
annotation.walkthrough: "Two" suggests a count of clergymen, but it stands for PRIME, since two is the smallest prime number.
annotation.definitionFit: Heads of government are the most senior figures in politics, so the plural definition fits the plural answer.

entries.clue: With members turning in work, we hear strike is over (5-5)

indicatorNotes.we hear: says the word for work out loud
indicatorNotes.is over: in a down clue, the strike sits over, above, the rest

blocks.note: to knock is to strike
to knead dough is to work it

annotation.surface: Union members going back to work; the strike has ended.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a union story, but the members are legs, and turning in is how knock-knees bend.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone knock-kneed has legs that curve inward so the knees touch.

entries.clue: Insights grasped by newspaper customers (7)

indicatorNotes.grasped by: the answer is held within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the second

annotation.surface: Newspaper buyers taking in some clever observations.
annotation.walkthrough: An aperçu is a French borrowing for a quick insight; the cedilla is dropped in the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: Aperçus are brief, illuminating insights or remarks.

entries.clue: Runner one must keep going after (7)

annotation.definition: Runner one must keep going after

blocks.note: the surface offers an athlete; a river is also a runner, since water runs
not chasing someone but having no way back once you have crossed

annotation.surface: An athlete you must keep chasing.
annotation.walkthrough: "Runner" suggests an athlete; it is a river, something that runs. Once Caesar crossed the Rubicon there was no turning back.
annotation.definitionFit: The Rubicon is the river whose crossing commits you to a course with no retreat.

entries.clue: Rallying can end on a volley (9)

indicatorNotes.Rallying: rallying is regrouping, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: these nine letters rearranged

annotation.surface: A tennis rally that may finish with a volley.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is tennis, but a volley here is many guns firing at once.
annotation.definitionFit: A cannonade is a sustained burst of artillery fire, a volley.

entries.clue: Losing capital, blames guarantees (7)

indicatorNotes.Losing capital: the capital, the first letter, is dropped

blocks.note: to censure is to blame
the first letter goes

annotation.surface: Someone who has lost money blames the guarantees given.
annotation.walkthrough: "Capital" suggests money or a city; here it is the head letter of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to guarantee it happens.

entries.clue: Classic song, maybe sister keeps private? (7)

blocks.note: Sr is the abbreviation for sister
an oldie is an old favourite, perhaps a song

annotation.surface: A nun who hides a favourite old song to herself.
annotation.walkthrough: "Keeps private" reads as keeping a secret; "private" is the definition, the lowest rank of soldier.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the lowest army rank names one kind of serviceman.

entries.clue: Virus regularly on BBC treated like the plague (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: takes every other letter of virus
indicatorNotes.treated: treated like medicine, the letters are worked over into a new order

blocks.note: v(I)r(U)s, the second and fourth letters
on as written
BBC as written

annotation.surface: A virus news story on the BBC, handled as if it were the plague.
annotation.walkthrough: The plague is the definition's own word, so "like the plague" means of the bubonic kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Bubonic plague is the best-known form of the plague, so bubonic describes it.

entries.clue: Meat’s first cut after bishop gives blessing (7)

indicatorNotes.first cut: the meat loses its first letter
indicatorNotes.after: what is left comes after the bishop

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
venison without its V

annotation.surface: A bishop blessing the meal after the first slice of the roast.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cut" fits the carving scene, but it is the instruction to remove venison's first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though archaic: the word comes via Old French from Latin benedictio, the same root as benediction.

entries.clue: Difficulty of acrobatics leads to big lumps in footwear (9,5)

indicatorNotes.leads to: takes the leading letters of big and lumps
indicatorNotes.in: those pieces go inside the footwear

blocks.note: tumbling is acrobatics
first letters of big and lumps
a sock is worn on the foot

annotation.surface: Tumbling is hard when it leaves big bruises in your shoes.
annotation.walkthrough: "Leads to" reads as causes, but it asks for the first letters of the next words.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from the Bible: something you trip over becomes any obstacle in your way.

entries.clue: Watch terms of reference being written up (5)

indicatorNotes.being written up: in a down clue, writing up puts the letters in reverse order

blocks.note: a remit is a set of terms of reference

annotation.surface: Keep an eye on the terms of reference as they are drafted.
annotation.walkthrough: "Watch" looks like a verb for monitoring; it is the noun, a timepiece.
annotation.definitionFit: A watch can serve as a timer, a device that measures time.

entries.clue: Revolutionary starter from flamboyant cook (4)

indicatorNotes.starter from: takes the first letter of flamboyant

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the revolutionary
first letter of flamboyant

annotation.surface: A flashy cook serving a radical new first course.
annotation.walkthrough: "Starter" fits the kitchen scene as a first course, but it means the opening letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though chef strictly means the head of a kitchen, from French chef de cuisine.

entries.clue: Great apes involved in his doom (9)

blocks.note: these nine letters rearranged

annotation.surface: Great apes playing a part in a man's downfall.
annotation.walkthrough: "In" looks like part of "involved in", but it is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose zoological fit: the superfamily takes in gorillas, chimps and orangutans, though also gibbons and humans.

entries.clue: A democrat wearing the First Lady’s skirt (5)

indicatorNotes.wearing: the first lady wraps around A and D like a garment

blocks.note: Eve was the first woman
A as written
D is short for Democrat

annotation.surface: A Democrat dressed in the President's wife's skirt.
annotation.walkthrough: "First Lady" suggests the US president's wife, which suits "democrat"; she is Eve. "Skirt" is the verb, to avoid.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb sense: to go round the edge of something rather than face it head on.

entries.clue: Patient meant to be carried (10)

blocks.note: the adjective: tolerant, slow to lose one's temper
split into two words: meant for, plus the act of carrying (to bear is to carry)

annotation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into FOR BEARING: intended for carrying.
annotation.definitionFit: Forbearing means patient and tolerant; something for bearing is meant to be carried.

entries.clue: Children surrender when caught (4)

indicatorNotes.when caught: to catch a word is to hear it, so we want its sound

blocks.note: to cede is to surrender

annotation.surface: Kids give up once they are caught.
annotation.walkthrough: "Caught" suggests capture; here it means heard. Seed for descendants is a biblical usage.
annotation.definitionFit: Seed means offspring or descendants, as in the seed of Abraham.
annotation.definitionNote: seed is a collective noun for offspring, standing in for the plural children
